newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India slides as local confidence slips.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India slides as local confidence slips.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) slid in thin trade as the local market dropped to a three-year low.
"We have not seen much stock coming out at these levels, but India is nobody's favourite market," said a trader.

The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed down 1.26 points, or 2.25 percent, at 54.78 points, with the premium over the local market contracting to 16.34 percent from yesterday's 16.90 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index fell 53.43 points, or 1.87 percent, to close at 2,798.0.
"People are just focusing on getting to the end of what looks like being a pretty miserable year," said the trader.

Gujarat Ambuja ended steady after Monday's hammering, at $6.25/$7.25, while Ashok Leyland fell again, losing 75 cents to $6.75/$7.75, Bajaj 80 cents to $25.75/$27.25 and Telco 50 cents to $8.25/$9.25.

The Capel Korea GDR Index ended down 1.86 points, or 2.85 percent, at 63.41, a premium of 28.71 percent over the local market, after the Korea Composite Index fell 2.24 points to a provisional 725.59.

The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended down 0.87 points, or 0.89 percent, at 96.64, a premium of 4.09 percent, after the Taiwan Weighted Index ended 46.42 points or 0.66 percent lower at 6,936.39. -- David Chance, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5887
